lines.trans: Good evening! How do you like our new cuisine?
May we invite the cook Katya here right now?
Good evening! Did you not like something today?
No, not at all, everything is simply great!
How does your dish hold its shape like that?
What is the secret? I can show you everything!
He said that there is old furniture here.
The guest will now go with me to the kitchen.
Nagiyev told Vika that the furniture needs to be changed.
Kostya, I am sure that Katya is lying.
You should have seen her face this afternoon!
She thinks that only she knows how to bluff.
Never mind, we have already been through this before!

examples.text: Спасибо, мы сегодня не хотим есть на улице.
examples.trans: Thank you, we do not want to eat on the street today.

examples.text: Уже два часа дня на улице!
examples.trans: It is already two o'clock in the afternoon outside!

examples.text: Ты бы видел её лицо сегодня днём!
examples.trans: You should have seen her face this afternoon!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне день начинается одинаково.
examples.trans: In our kitchen the day begins the same way.

examples.text: Любишь ты шутить каждый день.
examples.trans: You love to joke every day.

examples.text: Всё, Макс, теперь ты потерял деньги.
examples.trans: That is it, Max, now you have lost your money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'thinks', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Раньше ты так долго не думал.
examples.trans: Before, you did not take this long to think.

examples.text: Зачем вообще можно было такое придумать?
examples.trans: Why would anyone make up something like that at all?

examples.text: Я думаю, не надо пока менять.
examples.trans: I think we do not need to change anything yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

examples.text: Вокруг сейчас столько хорошего и красивого.
examples.trans: There is so much good and beautiful around right now.

examples.text: Она думает, что только она умеет играть.
examples.trans: She thinks that only she knows how to bluff.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'knows how to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Она думает, что только она умеет играть.
examples.trans: She thinks that only she knows how to bluff.

examples.text: Я умею плавать.
examples.trans: I can swim.

examples.text: Он не умеет считать.
examples.trans: He can't count.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to play', paired with 'сыграть'.

examples.text: Она думает, что только она умеет играть.
examples.trans: She thinks that only she knows how to bluff.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

examples.text: Дети играют во дворе.
examples.trans: The children are playing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего себе, какой большой шрам!
examples.trans: Wow, what a big scar!

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.
examples.trans: What do you want? Nothing, we are working.

examples.text: Шеф ничего не знает.
examples.trans: The chef knows nothing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы раньше долго работали вместе.
examples.trans: We used to work together for a long time.

examples.text: Его Нагиев привёл, это знакомый шефа.
examples.trans: Nagiyev brought him, he is an acquaintance of the chef.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это очень смешно, Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: That is very funny, Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Да, это было давно в армии.
examples.trans: Yes, that was a long time ago in the army.

examples.text: Это мой старый друг из Парижа.
examples.trans: This is my old friend from Paris.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф уже два месяца обещает меню.
examples.trans: The chef has been promising a menu for two months already.

examples.text: Ведь уже скоро лето закончится.
examples.trans: After all, summer will end soon.

examples.text: Ты уже стареешь, дорогой Витя?
examples.trans: Are you getting old already, dear Vitya?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'earlier', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Раньше ты так долго не думал.
examples.trans: Before, you did not take this long to think.

examples.text: Мы раньше долго работали вместе.
examples.trans: We used to work together for a long time.

examples.text: Ничего, мы это уже раньше проходили!
examples.trans: Never mind, we have already been through this before!

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Ничего, мы это уже раньше проходили!
examples.trans: Never mind, we have already been through this before!

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Come in, please.

examples.text: Проходи на кухню.
examples.trans: Come through to the kitchen.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.text: Шеф, да какой ещё может быть ребёнок?
examples.trans: Chef, what baby could there possibly be?

examples.text: Тогда у неё должны быть точные доказательства.
examples.trans: Then she must have exact proof.

examples.text: Подожди, но этого просто не может быть!
examples.trans: Wait, but this simply cannot be!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Нет, что вы, всё просто отлично!
examples.trans: No, not at all, everything is simply great!

examples.text: У меня есть отличный план!
examples.trans: I have a great plan!

examples.text: Не надо, Дима, я отлично работаю сам.
examples.trans: There is no need, Dima, I work great on my own.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда всю твою зарплату я забираю!
examples.trans: Then I am taking your entire paycheck!

examples.text: Берите хоть две мои зарплаты, шеф!
examples.trans: Take even two of my paychecks, Chef!

examples.text: Нет, давай сразу три зарплаты! Хорошо.
examples.trans: No, let us make it three paychecks right away! Deal.
